summary: Bitterroot NF crude pole platform built in the 1930s and abandoned in the 1940s; firelookout.com pages disagree on whether it collapsed in 2021/22 or still stands.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says it collapsed in the winter of 2021/2022; a second firelookout.com page says it is still there

events.note: Built in the 1930s; the year is a decade only
Collapsed in the winter of 2021/2022, per firelookout.com

evidence.supports: about ten miles east of Stevensville
managed by the Bitterroot National Forest
rough pole platform about 30 feet tall, built in the 1930s; abandoned in the 1940s
evidence.quote: This crude 30' pole platform, built in the 1930's, was abandoned in the 1940's.

evidence.supports: stood until the winter of 2021 to 2022, then collapsed
evidence.quote: It remained standing until the winter of 2021/2022 when it collapsed.

evidence.supports: a second page says the platform is still there
listed as type platform, status Abandoned, at 46.50331 north and 113.88190 west
photos credited to the Fire Lookout Museum and Gary Little
evidence.quote: Photos courtesy the Fire Lookout Museum and Gary Little

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com's main page says the platform collapsed in the winter of 2021/2022; its order page says it is still there. The story reports both and does not choose. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list says Abandoned, not gone. The record's gone status rests on the collapse account.

notes_for_editor: Basic facts (1930s build, 1940s abandonment, Bitterroot NF, location) agree across the firelookout.com pages; the collapse versus still-there conflict is unresolved. The Weebly page (montanalookouts.weebly.com/ambrose-point.html) pairs the name with a USGS 1957 survey datasheet for station AMBROSE (PID RX1016) that mentions a 36 ft wooden tower built to clear stations through lodgepole pine. No source says that survey tower is the lookout, so it is not used. No source gives access, staffing or visit details. The firelookout.com photo credit (Fire Lookout Museum, Gary Little) has no image URL in the cached text, so no photos added. Brief record checked: county, agency, kind (platform) and coordinates match the sources.
